Trust is a perennial problem among the Tin Foil Hat Club. How do we keep the discussion from being astroturfed? One answer might be to make a secret club. A Tin Foiled Order. With a special handshake so we know who's trustworthy. We can all wear our Tin Foil Hats in different ways to show how much or little we've woken up from the collective trance. I'd like to see this subverse address this question a bit. For about the past... three? years, accusations and claims of "shill" have been proliferating -- and not without reason. At the same time, some of us (cough ... wikileaks) would like to remain anon. I think we should address this issue.

Here's the thing, part of what's exciting is sifting through the BS. Some of it's funny. Some of it's so awesomely funny it helps me bring up conspiracy talk in day to day discourse. Some of it just amazes me that someone had the conviction to see research through on such unplausible ideas. As an example, everyone at my office is now on the lookout for lizard people.

Finally, we need to keep business interests on the business end of things and communications on a shole other planet. Half the fights between notable theorists are the same as any modern day competition - he/she deserves more/less attention.

Where do we start? Civility, even under the worst of circumstances.
